prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1255; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss for the left-turn collision. Insured reports the other vehicle came through the opposing lane while insured was turning across traffic. Police report requested. Claimant has retained counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation and request the claimant's medical authorization forms. Counsel stated the claimant is experiencing neck and back strain and is following a treatment plan. Asked for itemized medical bills and treatment notes before evaluating the bodily injury component.

Entry 3: Received the responding officer's report. It notes the insured was turning left at an intersection and the other driver was traveling straight through on a green signal. Photos of both vehicles show front-end damage to the insured's vehicle and driver-side damage to the claimant's vehicle. Witness statement still outstanding.

Entry 4: Obtained a recorded statement from the insured, who confirms they looked for oncoming traffic but did not see the other vehicle until the impact. Insured has no prior claims on this policy. Scheduled a field inspection of both vehicles and sent repair estimates to the appraiser for review.

Entry 5: Received updated records from claimant's counsel showing a physical therapy referral for neck and back strain, with ongoing sessions expected. Coordinated with the bodily injury unit to set a review point once treatment notes are complete. Diary set to follow up with counsel for the outstanding witness contact and final medical summary.
